references.text: God gives food to the ravens. [ref:Job 38:41|Job 38:41]: "Who provides food for the raven when its young cry out to God?" Jesus points to the ravens as an example of God's care, and this directly connects to the book of Job where God Himself highlights His care for the ravens.

[ref:Sal 147:9|Psalm 147:9]: "He gives food to the animals, to the young ravens that cry out." The same theme as in Luke 12:24 – God provides for the ravens, and this is used as a basis for trusting His care for people.

Parallel passage in the Sermon on the Mount. [ref:Matt 6:26|Matthew 6:26]: "Look at the birds of the air! They do not sow or reap or gather into barns, yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not much more valuable than they?" This is the Matthean parallel to Jesus' teaching about not worrying.

[ref:Matt 10:31|Matthew 10:31]: "So do not be afraid! You are worth more than many sparrows." The same principle: human value surpasses that of birds in God's eyes, giving reason for trust rather than worry.

[ref:Matt 6:28-30|Matthew 6:28-30] continues the same argument with the lilies of the field. God clothes the grass that is here today and thrown into the oven tomorrow – "will He not much more clothe you, you of little faith?" The argument from the lesser to the greater ("how much more") is the same as in Luke 12:24.
[ref:Luk 12:7|Luke 12:7]: "You are worth more than many sparrows." Earlier in the same chapter, Jesus uses a similar argument about God's care for birds as a basis for human value and security.

[ref:Luk 12:27-28|Luke 12:27-28] follows up with the lilies as a parallel example: they do not labor or spin, yet Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one of them. The same "how much more" argument as in verse 24.
[ref:1 Pet 5:7|1 Peter 5:7]: "Cast all your anxiety on Him, for He cares for you." Peter's exhortation builds on the same trust in God's care that Jesus teaches in Luke 12:24.

[ref:Fil 4:6-7|Philippians 4:6-7]: "Do not be anxious about anything! But present everything to God in prayer." Paul's exhortation against anxiety aligns with Jesus' words about considering the ravens and trusting in God's provision.

[ref:1 Mos 8:7|Genesis 8:7]: Noah sent out a raven from the ark. The raven is a well-known motif in the OT, and Jesus chooses precisely the raven – an unclean bird – to emphasize that even the least valued creature receives food from God.
